title: Linux Labs Final Assessment
instructions: Complete each task in order or skip between sections. Sixty-five points come from typed answers checked against this browser's answer key; this does not execute or prove a Linux command. Thirty-five points are learner-reported practical checks: run those commands yourself in the repository playground, then confirm the rubric items you verified. The assessment never runs shell commands and does not touch host files.
prerequisites: Complete or review the five learning stages
Initialize the synthetic playground with setup/setup.sh
Use a Linux terminal for practical tasks; the browser cannot verify command execution

sections.title: A. Command fundamentals and syntax
sections.description: Choose commands and paths precisely, and recognize a safer interactive option.

tasks.prompt: Which command searches the directories in PATH to locate an executable?
tasks.hint: The command name is also one of the Stage 03 lessons.
tasks.feedback: Use which to report the executable selected from PATH. whereis searches a wider set of related locations.

tasks.prompt: From the repository root, enter the relative path to the synthetic employee dataset.
tasks.feedback: The dataset is under playground/data/ and is safe synthetic data.

tasks.prompt: Which rm option asks before removing each file? Enter the short option.
tasks.feedback: rm -i prompts for confirmation. Always inspect and tightly scope deletion targets; never practice against system paths.

sections.title: B. File system operations
sections.description: Practice creating, copying, moving, checking, and safely cleaning files in the marked disposable organization workspace.

tasks.prompt: Inside playground/projects/organization-lab only, create assessment/ready, copy inbox/launch-checklist.txt into it as review-checklist.txt, and verify the source and copy are present.
tasks.hint: Use mkdir -p, cp, pwd, and ls. Quote any path that contains spaces.
tasks.feedback: This is self-assessed: the app records your checklist, not command execution.
rubric: I confirmed the working tree is playground/projects/organization-lab.
The copied file exists and the original remains in inbox.

tasks.prompt: Create one temporary note under the marked organization-lab directory, inspect the exact target, and remove only that file with an interactive confirmation. Verify the workspace remains intact.
tasks.hint: Use a fully quoted, explicit path and ls before rm -i. Do not use rm -r or a wildcard.
tasks.feedback: This is self-assessed: the app does not inspect your filesystem. The reset script can restore the marked starter workspace.
tasks.solution:
target='playground/projects/organization-lab/assessment/temp note.txt'
printf 'temporary
' > "$target"
ls -l -- "$target"
rm -i -- "$target"
bash setup/reset-lab.sh --yes
bash setup/setup.sh
rubric: I inspected the single exact file before deletion and used rm -i without recursion or a wildcard.
I verified the workspace and used the documented playground reset workflow afterward.

sections.title: C. File content inspection and search
sections.description: Select appropriate readers, investigate the synthetic authentication log, and locate a configuration-like fixture.

tasks.prompt: Which command is the best interactive pager for navigating a large log without printing the whole file?
tasks.hint: It lets you search and move both forward and backward.
tasks.feedback: less is a pager designed for navigating large files. cat writes the whole file to standard output.

tasks.prompt: The synthetic auth.log has two lines containing the exact phrase Failed password. What does grep -c 'Failed password' playground/logs/auth.log return? Enter the number.
tasks.hint: Count matching lines, not words or unique IP addresses.
tasks.feedback: There are two failed-password events in the synthetic fixture.

tasks.prompt: Use find to locate regular files named *.conf under playground/projects. Confirm the result stays inside the repository playground.
tasks.hint: Combine a bounded starting directory with -type f and -name.
tasks.feedback: This is self-assessed: the browser checks your confirmation only.
rubric: I used playground/projects as the search root and selected regular files with -type f.
The result was playground/projects/atlas/config/app.conf and I did not search or modify system paths.

sections.title: D. Text processing and pipelines
sections.description: Combine commands and reason about deterministic synthetic CSV and log results.

tasks.prompt: Using the transactions CSV, awk -F, 'NR > 1 && $6 == "complete" { total += $5 } END { printf "%.2f\n", total }' returns what total amount for complete transactions? Enter the number only.
tasks.hint: Sum the amount column only where the status column is complete; skip the header.
tasks.feedback: The complete rows have amounts 12.75, 5.00, and 37.00, totaling 54.75.
tasks.solution: awk -F, 'NR > 1 && $6 == "complete" { total += $5 } END { printf "%.2f\n", total }' playground/data/transactions.csv

tasks.prompt: How many active employees are in employees.csv, excluding the header?
tasks.hint: There are five data rows; one is inactive.
tasks.feedback: Four of the five synthetic employee rows have status active.
tasks.solution: awk -F, 'NR > 1 && $5 == "active" { count++ } END { print count+0 }' playground/data/employees.csv

tasks.prompt: Complete the pipeline: cut -d, -f3 playground/data/employees.csv | ____ | uniq -c. What command must sort the values so all duplicate departments are adjacent?
tasks.hint: uniq compares adjacent lines; the input begins in original CSV order.
tasks.feedback: Sort the extracted fields before uniq so duplicates are adjacent and can be counted globally.

sections.title: E. System information and resource investigation
sections.description: Choose the right tool and interpret what it measures without relying on fixed live machine values.

tasks.prompt: Which command and option display memory values in human-readable units? Enter both, for example: free -h
tasks.feedback: free -h reports host memory in readable units. Its values vary while the system runs.

tasks.prompt: Which command estimates the space used by a directory tree: df or du?
tasks.hint: Its name refers to disk usage for files/directories.
tasks.feedback: du estimates file and directory usage. df reports capacity and usage for mounted filesystems.

sections.title: F. Integrated practical scenario
sections.description: Triage synthetic service and authentication records, summarize business data, and inspect resource usage with safe, composed commands.

tasks.prompt: Complete the integrated investigation from the repository root. Work only with the synthetic playground. Find the application error count, summarize failed-auth source IPs, calculate complete transaction value, locate the app.conf fixture, compare filesystem capacity with playground directory size, inspect a live process snapshot, and time one read-only command. Write down the commands and short findings in your notes.
tasks.hint: Use grep and wc for counts; grep, awk, sort, and uniq for IP summaries; awk for the CSV total; find for app.conf; df and du answer different questions. top metrics and time measurements vary, so explain what they mean rather than recording fixed values.
tasks.feedback: This scenario is self-assessed. The app records your rubric completion and does not inspect files, execute commands, or assert live system values.
tasks.solution:
grep -i -c 'ERROR' playground/logs/app.log
grep 'Failed password' playground/logs/auth.log | awk '{print $11}' | sort | uniq -c
awk -F, 'NR > 1 && $6 == "complete" { total += $5 } END { printf "%.2f\n", total }' playground/data/transactions.csv
find playground/projects -type f -name '*.conf'
df -hT .
du -sh playground
top -b -n 1 | head -n 10
time grep -i -c 'ERROR' playground/logs/app.log
rubric: The application log error count is 1, and I used a bounded read-only search.
The auth summary has two failed events, one each from 192.0.2.10 and 198.51.100.23.
The complete transaction total is 54.75 and app.conf was found under playground/projects/atlas/config/.
I used df for filesystem capacity and du for playground directory usage, and kept all operations read-only and within the playground.
I inspected top output as live host data and interpreted time's real elapsed, user CPU, and system CPU values without expecting fixed measurements.
